name: cmux AI Agents Bundle
description: Skills, hook scripts, recipes, and prompts for orchestrating AI coding agents inside cmux. Free, MIT.

plugins.name: cmux Control Skill
plugins.description: Full cmux CLI + socket API skill for Claude Code — workspaces, panes, surfaces, browser automation, notifications, sidebar metadata, session restore.

plugins.name: Notify on Build Fail
plugins.description: Runs your build command and fires a cmux system notification when it fails. Zero-config drop-in for any project.

plugins.name: Flash on Test Pass
plugins.description: Triggers a blue-ring attention flash on the workspace when your test suite passes, so you notice without watching the pane.

plugins.name: Screenshot Browser Surface
plugins.description: Takes a screenshot of a cmux WKWebView browser surface and saves it to disk. Useful for visual regression checks inside agent workflows.

plugins.name: Spawn Focus-Neutral Helper Pane
plugins.description: Opens a right-side helper pane in the caller's workspace without stealing focus. Safe to call from any agent hook.

plugins.name: Send Text to Another Surface
plugins.description: Routes a shell command or text to a specific surface by ref (e.g. surface:7) without switching focus.

plugins.name: Tail Vercel Deploy with Status Pill
plugins.description: Watches a Vercel deployment and updates the sidebar status pill in real time — building → ready or error.

plugins.name: Three Agents on One PR
plugins.description: Spawns three parallel Claude Code agent panes in the same workspace — reviewer, implementer, and tester — all anchored to a single PR branch.

plugins.name: Sidebar Progress Bar from Script
plugins.description: Pipes any script's 0–100 output lines into the cmux sidebar progress bar. Works with any build, migration, or batch job.

plugins.name: Sticky Sidebar Status Pill
plugins.description: Sets a persistent color-coded status label on the workspace sidebar — useful for displaying environment, branch state, or agent status.

plugins.name: Open Markdown in Live Viewer
plugins.description: Opens a .md file in the cmux live-watching Markdown renderer in a new right-side pane, so documentation updates are visible as you write.

plugins.name: Browser Fill & Submit Form
plugins.description: Opens a URL, waits for load, fills form fields by element ref, and submits — full WKWebView browser automation from a shell script.

plugins.name: Poll Socket for Surface Events
plugins.description: Connects to /tmp/cmux.sock via JSON-RPC and polls a surface for new output lines. Low-overhead event loop for shell-based watchers.

plugins.name: Detect cmux Context
plugins.description: Guards any script with a cmux presence check using CMUX_WORKSPACE_ID and the socket path. Drop this at the top of any hook script.

plugins.name: Minimal Python JSON-RPC Client
plugins.description: Two-function Python snippet for talking to /tmp/cmux.sock — send any JSON-RPC v2 method and parse the response. No dependencies beyond stdlib.

plugins.name: Batch Rename Workspaces by CWD
plugins.description: Loops over all open workspaces and renames each one to the basename of its working directory. Tidies up after a busy session.

plugins.name: Auto Flash on Stale PR
plugins.description: Polls GitHub for PRs that have gone stale (no activity in N days) and triggers a workspace flash to prompt the agent to follow up.

plugins.name: Open SSH Remote Workspace
plugins.description: Creates a new cmux workspace with an SSH connection to a remote VPS as the default shell, then optionally launches an agent inside it.

plugins.name: Browser Wait for Element
plugins.description: Waits for a CSS selector to appear in a WKWebView surface before the next automation step. Prevents flaky timing errors in browser scripts.

plugins.name: Agent Handoff Notification
plugins.description: Sends a cmux notification when one agent finishes and passes context to the next — useful in multi-agent pipelines where agents hand off work sequentially.

plugins.name: Restore Session on Boot
plugins.description: Calls cmux session restore from a login script (e.g. ~/.zprofile), so your full agent workspace layout is rebuilt automatically after a reboot.
